statement: Relative employment index of ages 22-25 in the most AI-exposed occupation quintile falls >= 5 pts from its 2026 level (Stanford Digital Economy Lab 'Canaries' series, last 2027 release)
status_at_phase_end: The named series did not exist in 2024 (first circulated Aug 2025). Evidence on early-career / exposed-occupation employment in 2024 came only from online-freelance-platform studies: modest declines (~2% contracts, ~5% earnings) for writing-type freelancers after the first mass-market chatbot launch, and ~20-30% fewer job posts in automation-prone writing/coding categories, with reduced demand for novices. Payroll-based age-by-exposure evidence was not yet public.

items.summary: No age-by-AI-exposure payroll employment index was published during 2024; the indicator's source series begins in 2025. Bloc B has no comparable series.
items.detail: Brynjolfsson, Chandar & Chen 'Canaries in the Coal Mine?' first circulated Aug 2025 (ADP data, Bloc A). Its back-cast values for 2024 are later-published and excluded under the as-of rule.

items.summary: Peer-reviewed study of a large online freelance platform: after the first mass-market chatbot launch, freelancers in the most exposed (writing-related) occupations saw ~2% fewer monthly contracts and ~5% lower monthly earnings; declines were larger, not smaller, for higher-skilled freelancers. Proxy evidence only (freelancers, not age-specific).
items.detail: Hui, Reshef & Zhou, 'The Short-Term Effects of Generative Artificial Intelligence on Employment: Evidence from an Online Labor Market', Organization Science 2024 (doi 10.1287/orsc.2023.18441), Upwork data. Online publication day approximate (2024); working paper since Aug 2023.

items.summary: Working paper on online freelancing: job posts for automation-prone writing and coding work fell ~21% relative to manual-intensive jobs after the chatbot launch (writing ~30%), and image-creation posts ~17% after image-generator launches. Proxy for entry-level knowledge-work demand.
items.detail: Demirci, Hannane & Zhu, 'Who Is AI Replacing? The Impact of Generative AI on Online Freelancing Platforms', presented at Platform Strategy Research Symposium (June 2024; day approximate), later in Management Science.

items.summary: Journal article on freelancer demand: postings in skill clusters substitutable by generative AI fell ~7% overall (20-50% for writing and translation clusters), while complementary clusters such as programming grew; demand for novice workers fell even in complementary clusters.
items.detail: Teutloff et al., 'Winners and losers of generative AI: Early Evidence of Shifts in Freelancer Demand', Journal of Economic Behavior & Organization (ScienceDirect S0167268124004591; online ~Dec 2024, date approximate).
